findings.where: First screen, the action row under the second paragraph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: There are two filled blue buttons, 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation', the same size and weight, with the email address set between them. They share one look and sit equally close, so no single action wins. The address could belong to either button.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer ready to contact Mark has to choose between two equal routes without knowing how they differ. The founder asked for one direct, personal way to reach him, and the brief's research calls for one action on the first screen.

findings.where: First screen, the tracked all-capitals paragraph under the heading ('I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…')
findings.fault: Squint and this four-line block of bold, tracked capitals is the second-loudest thing on the screen. It reads as a second heading and draws the eye ahead of the photograph and the action. Together with a second serif paragraph and three margin notes, the hero carries two statements where it should carry one message.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for who Mark is and how to reach him hits a dense shouted block. The founder wants refined, not busy, and Mark finds busy sites off-putting (brand sheet §6).

findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph in the right column (desktop)
findings.fault: The photograph floats. Its top sits about 120 px below the heading's first line, and its bottom lines up with neither paragraph nor the action row, so it ties to no line of the text column beside it. It reads as placed loosely rather than set as a framed exhibit.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges the first screen first. A direction whose whole idea is a well-set brief loses that idea when its one exhibit sits off the grid.

findings.where: Header, the logo mark at the left
findings.fault: The 'MMM INFRA' lettering under the arches sits almost on the header's bottom edge, where the hero's tinted band begins. The mark looks cramped and clipped against the band, while the name and nav beside it have generous room.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, for whom the logo sits beside his name as part of the identity. Cramming it against an edge makes the lockup look careless.

findings.where: Phone, first screen and the action group at the end of the hero
findings.fault: The action only appears after the heading, a margin note, the photograph, the capitals paragraph, a second note, the second paragraph and a third note, roughly a screen and a half down. When it comes, 'Book a consultation' is indented from the left edge that everything else holds, and the email address sits flush on top of that button rather than with 'Write to me'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone, often an officer between meetings, cannot reach Mark without scrolling past the whole hero. When they get there, the address seems to label the wrong button and the button looks misaligned.

findings.fault: The section splits into two columns that do not line up. The curve and its note sit at the top left. The exhibit photo, 'Replay the entrance' and the timing table start about 600 px lower in the right column. That leaves roughly 400 px of empty paper under the curve, and the replay control is cut off from the sketch it replays. The staggered columns break continuity, and the section does not read as one unit.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark reviewing the motion sketch have to hunt for the replay control and the photo it moves. The stagger looks like a layout fault, not intent.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lead-in 'With a new PPP Act, the country can:' and its list; the image caption
findings.fault: The lead-in sentence is separated from its own list by a full paragraph gap, while the subhead above sits almost touching its paragraph, so the spacing does not group what belongs together. The caption's 'Placeholder…' runs on after the italic caption at a loose line height, and its last words wrap to a stray second line.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who must publish articles in this pattern: the specimen is meant to prove the rhythm holds with a subhead, a list and a captioned image, and here the list detaches from its lead-in. A reader sees the list as a new thought.

findings.where: Whole page grid, right edges: nav, hero photo and footer rule vs. palette swatches and motion table
findings.fault: The right edge changes from section to section. The nav, hero photograph and footer rule end at about 1368 px, the palette swatches and the timing table at about 1320 px. The logo and footer start further left than the margin-note column. The page has no single outer frame.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for refined rather than slapdash. In a direction modelled on a well-set journal, edges that drift read as unfinished.
